name: Why Do We Need Weight Decay in Modern Deep Learning?
summary: Argues that weight decay acts through the training dynamics rather than as an explicit regularizer, for vision models trained with SGD and for language models trained about one epoch.

name: Accurate, Large Minibatch SGD: Training ImageNet in 1 Hour
summary: Trains ResNet-50 on ImageNet with minibatches of 8192 images by scaling the learning rate linearly with the batch size and warming it up.

name: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
summary: Introduces residual networks, in which stacked layers learn residual functions with identity shortcut connections, allowing much deeper networks to be trained.

name: Bag of Tricks for Image Classification with Convolutional Neural Networks
summary: Collects training refinements and small changes to the ResNet architecture, among them moving the stride of the downsampling block, and measures their effect.

name: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
summary: Describes a large deep convolutional network trained on ImageNet with ReLUs, GPU training, data augmentation and dropout in the fully connected layers.

name: A Simple Weight Decay Can Improve Generalization
summary: Shows for linear networks that weight decay improves generalization by suppressing irrelevant components of the weight vector and part of the effect of static noise on the targets.
venue: NIPS 1991 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 4)

name: An Exponential Learning Rate Schedule for Deep Learning
summary: Proves that for normalized networks, SGD with momentum and weight decay is equivalent to SGD with momentum, no weight decay and an exponentially increasing learning rate.

name: Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization
summary: Shows that L2 regularization and weight decay differ for adaptive optimizers such as Adam, and proposes AdamW, which decouples the weight decay from the gradient-based update.

name: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
summary: Describes LLaMA, decoder-only language models of 7B to 65B parameters trained only on publicly available data, with their architecture, training data and benchmark results.

name: L2 Regularization versus Batch and Weight Normalization
summary: Shows that with batch or weight normalization an L2 penalty has no regularizing effect, and that it instead changes the effective learning rate of the weights.

name: Three Mechanisms of Weight Decay Regularization
summary: Identifies three ways weight decay regularizes, depending on optimizer and architecture: a larger effective learning rate, an approximate Jacobian penalty, and smaller effective damping in second-order methods.
